items.front: India's latitudinal/longitudinal extent and IST meridian?
items.examPoint: Location & extent — 8°4'–37°6'N, 68°7'–97°25'E, Tropic of Cancer, IST 82.5°E

items.front: India's longest land border neighbour, and coastline length?
items.back: Bangladesh (4,096 km) longest; total land border ~15,200 km; coastline 7,516.6 km.
items.examPoint: Size, land border (15,200 km), coastline (7,516.6 km) & neighbours

items.front: Northernmost vs southernmost point of India (don't confuse)?
items.back: Northernmost = Indira Col (Siachen); southernmost = Indira Point (Great Nicobar).
items.examPoint: Extremities — Indira Col vs Indira Point; N-S 3,214 km, E-W 2,933 km

items.front: Himalayan longitudinal ranges N→S and highest peak wholly in India?
items.back: Trans-Himalaya → Himadri → Himachal → Shiwalik. Highest wholly in India = Kanchenjunga (8,586 m).
Eastern extension of Himalayas forming India's east border: Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo (Lushai) hills.

items.front: Northern Plains belts N→S and the most fertile?
items.back: Bhabar (pebbly) → Terai (marshy) → Bhangar (old, kankar) → Khadar (new floodplain, most fertile).

items.front: Vindhya vs Satpura position relative to Narmada/Tapi?
items.back: Vindhya north of the Narmada; Satpura between the Narmada and Tapi (peak Dhupgarh 1,350 m).
items.examPoint: Vindhya vs Satpura ranges; Western & Eastern Ghats

items.front: Western vs Eastern Coastal Plain — coast type?
items.back: Western = submergent (natural harbours, narrow, Konkan/Malabar); Eastern = emergent (wider, deltaic, Coromandel).
items.examPoint: Coastal Plains — Western (submergent) vs Eastern (emergent); Konkan/Coromandel

items.front: Origin of Andaman-Nicobar vs Lakshadweep islands?
items.back: Andaman-Nicobar = volcanic/tectonic (Barren = only active volcano); Lakshadweep = coral atolls.
East (deltas, Bay of Bengal): Godavari/Krishna/Kaveri/Mahanadi. West (estuaries, Arabian Sea): Narmada, Tapi.

items.front: What is an antecedent river (with examples)?
items.back: A river older than the uplift that keeps its course by cutting gorges — Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra across the Himalayas.
items.examPoint: Drainage concepts — basin/watershed, patterns, antecedent vs consequent

items.front: SW monsoon triggers; where does NE monsoon rain?
items.back: Tibetan low + STJ northward shift + Tropical Easterly Jet + Somali jet. NE monsoon rains Coromandel coast & coastal AP (Oct–Dec).
items.examPoint: SW monsoon mechanism — Tibetan low, jet streams (STJ/TEJ), onset

items.front: Black soil use; most widespread forest type in India?
items.back: Black (regur) soil = cotton on Deccan Trap. Most widespread forest = tropical (moist/dry) deciduous — sal & teak.
items.examPoint: Soils of India — alluvial/black/red/laterite/desert & associated crops

items.front: India's first NP, Project Tiger year, largest NP, faunal strongholds?
items.back: Jim Corbett (1936, first); Project Tiger 1973; Hemis largest. Gir lion, Kaziranga rhino, Little Rann wild ass, Dachigam hangul.
items.examPoint: National parks & tiger reserves — first NP (Jim Corbett), Project Tiger (1973), distribution
